title: Publish 0.6.2 to npm — tagged, qualified and receipt-verified; awaiting the user's authorisation
description:
0.6.2 is tagged, qualified and receipt-verified. ONLY the npm publish remains, and it needs a HUMAN AT A REAL TERMINAL -- npm demands a browser OTP that cannot complete in a non-TTY. Do not attempt it from an agent session.

=== ALREADY VERIFIED. DO NOT RE-DERIVE OR RE-RUN ANY OF THIS ===

  Tag v0.6.2            -> commit ea3813ae39fd9c9bba1e5e24e32a4c73e1611480
  That commit is the tip main was promoted to, and remains an ancestor of main.
  Qualification run      34801853367 (attempt 3), conclusion: success
  Receipt                schema lore.ladybug-qualification-evidence/1
                         repository.commit = ea3813ae39fd9c9bba1e5e24e32a4c73e1611480
                         status = pass
  Receipt verified INDEPENDENTLY, not merely read: the concurrency evidence
  artifact was downloaded and its sha256 recomputed as
  dae6a2773720be84676dce3da57ac37db4c90979b58935e662c3c817b569b70a,
  which matches the digest the receipt claims, byte for byte. A self-consistent
  receipt proves nothing about what was built; this one attests real bytes from
  the shipped commit.
  The LCLI-481 provenance gate ran and behaved: --pre success on every attempt,
  --post correctly skipped because nothing published.

These are settled facts. A successor re-running qualification would burn ~25
minutes to learn what is written above.

=== THE PUBLISH, READY TO PASTE ===

The artifacts are NOT on disk, and CI does NOT produce SHA256SUMS.txt -- the
operator generates it (see the WARNING below about what that check does and does
not prove).

    cd /Volumes/external/repos/lore-cli
    gh run download 34801853367 -n npm-packages -D scripts/release-0.6.2
    cd scripts/release-0.6.2 && shasum -a 256 *.tgz > SHA256SUMS.txt && cd -
    ls scripts/release-0.6.2/*.tgz | wc -l          # must be 7
    scripts/publish-release.sh 0.6.2 34801853367 --dry-run    # rehearse; touches nothing
    scripts/publish-release.sh 0.6.2 34801853367              # the real publish

AUTH -- THIS PARAGRAPH WAS CORRECTED 2026-09-14. What it used to say, and how the
correction was established, is preserved in this task's implementation note; nothing has
been removed from the record. What is ACTUALLY on this machine, from a presence-only
inspection that printed no values and changed nothing:

    Keychain service npm-opum-ai-publish : ABSENT (security find-generic-password exits 44)
    NPM_TOKEN                            : NOT SET
    ~/.npmrc                             : EXISTS, carries //registry.npmjs.org/:_authToken

So the publish authenticates from publish-release.sh's LAST fallback, ~/.npmrc -- not from
the Keychain token the script is designed around. `npm login` writes exactly that
_authToken line, and a web-login session stays subject to require-2FA-on-write, which the
script's own header names as the EOTP wall the Keychain token exists to bypass. That is the
most likely explanation for the browser OTP. It is an inference from the configuration, not
a measurement of the prompt.

WHAT THIS MEANS IF YOU ARE ABOUT TO PUBLISH: expect the OTP prompt and expect to need a
person at a TTY -- but do NOT expect a different token type to fix it. Per
docs/runbooks/release-publishing.md:557-565, npm revoked every classic token on 9 December
2025, leaving granular access tokens as the only kind (90-day cap, 2FA-bound, website-only
creation). Setting up a working unattended token is a CREDENTIAL CHANGE: it belongs to the
user directly and is not something to attempt in order to get tonight's publish through.

NOT ESTABLISHED: whether the ~/.npmrc token is a granular access token or a web-login
session token. Reading it would not distinguish them (both are npm_-prefixed). `npm whoami`
would -- a 401 means expired or revoked rather than 2FA-gated -- but it authenticates as the
user and was outside the presence-only scope authorised. Follow-on work: LCLI-489.

ORDERING IS LOAD-BEARING: six platform packages first, root launcher LAST, so the
launcher is never resolvable before the binary it execs. Fail-closed -- a
platform failure stops BEFORE the launcher, so a partial publish leaves nothing
installable and the same version can be retried. Resumable: an already-published
package is skipped rather than re-attempted.

AFTER PUBLISHING, DO NOT PANIC AT A SLOW REGISTRY. LCLI-460 shipped in this
release: the script now waits up to 30 minutes with backoff before the install
smoke and states explicitly that a timeout is NOT proof the publish failed. The
lag is real and worsening -- 0.4.5 ~15s, 0.4.6 ~35s, 0.5.0 ~25 MINUTES. NEVER
reach for `npm unpublish` on a propagation delay; it is destructive, available
for 72 hours, and the wrong tool for this.

=== WARNING: THE DIGEST CHECK IS CIRCULAR ===

publish-release.sh advertises "verifies every tarball's sha256 against
SHA256SUMS.txt BEFORE publishing anything". CI never emits that file, so the
operator generates it from the very tarballs it then verifies. That proves only
that the files have not changed since `shasum` ran -- NOT that they are the
qualified artifacts. Treat the check as a tamper-evidence seal on your own
download, not as provenance. Making it real needs digests CI recorded
independently. Not yet filed as a task; it needs a decision about the source of
truth, not just an edit.

=== AFTER A SUCCESSFUL PUBLISH ===

1. Update the post-publish evidence, which was deliberately NOT touched at bump
   time because both files state what is published NOW: README.md and
   docs/reference/lore-cli-release-truth.md.
2. Cut a GitHub Release for v0.6.2 using CHANGELOG.md's [0.6.2] section.
3. Tell opum-marketplace that npm dist-tags.latest has actually moved. They are
   deliberately HOLDING their opum-lore pin at v0.6.1 until it does, because
   pinning ahead of npm would point the skill at a release nobody can install.
   They already have the skills/ tree SHA 24277e9a94d6cc9b5a8c7fa12fa32c4f15eb4c0f
   and have recorded in their own memory to check `npm view @opum-ai/lore
   dist-tags` themselves rather than wait for a message.
4. 0.6.2 ships with NO provenance attestation, as 0.6.1 did (LCLI-482, open).
   Say so wherever the release is announced rather than letting someone find it
   in the packument and read it as tampering.

acceptanceCriteria.text: A published @opum-ai/lore 0.6.2 exists on the registry with dist-tags.latest at 0.6.2, verified by `npm view @opum-ai/lore dist-tags` rather than by the publish command exiting 0
All seven packages are live -- the six platform packages and the root launcher -- and a clean-registry `npx --yes @opum-ai/lore@0.6.2 --version` reports 0.6.2
README.md and docs/reference/lore-cli-release-truth.md are updated to state 0.6.2 as the published version, which was deliberately deferred from the bump because they assert what is published now
A GitHub Release exists for v0.6.2 carrying CHANGELOG.md 0.6.2 section
opum-marketplace is told that dist-tags.latest actually moved, so it can lift its deliberate hold at v0.6.1
The release is recorded as having shipped WITHOUT a provenance attestation, so nobody later reads the absence as tampering (LCLI-482 remains open)

implementationNotes:
AUTH DESCRIPTION IN THIS RECORD IS WRONG — CORRECTED 2026-09-14, before any fourth publish attempt.

This task says auth is "a granular or automation npm token read from the macOS Keychain (service
npm-opum-ai-publish), falling back to NPM_TOKEN then ~/.npmrc". Checked on this machine, with the
user's explicit go-ahead for a presence-only inspection that printed no values:

  - Keychain service npm-opum-ai-publish : ABSENT. `security find-generic-password -s
    npm-opum-ai-publish` exits 44, "could not be found in the keychain".
  - NPM_TOKEN                            : NOT SET.
  - ~/.npmrc                             : EXISTS and contains //registry.npmjs.org/:_authToken
                                           (plus //npm.pkg.github.com/:_authToken, an
                                           @evolvconsulting:registry line, and allow-scripts).

So both documented primary paths are unused. The publish authenticates with whatever token sits in
~/.npmrc — the script's LAST fallback, not its designed one.

WHY THAT LIKELY EXPLAINS THE OTP WALL, stated as the inference it is rather than as a measurement.
`npm login` writes exactly that `//registry.npmjs.org/:_authToken` line, and a web-login session
remains subject to "require 2FA for writes". publish-release.sh:5-8 names this precisely as the EOTP
wall the Keychain token exists to bypass. An unattended publish was therefore never actually
configured on this machine — the OTP prompt is the documented behaviour of the fallback that is in
use, not a surprise.

NOT ESTABLISHED, and it is the question that decides whether the wall is removable: whether that
~/.npmrc token is a granular access token or a web-login session token. Reading the token would not
settle it either (both carry the npm_ prefix). The decisive read-only checks are `npm whoami` — a 401
would mean expired or revoked rather than 2FA-gated — or simply looking at npmjs.com. Neither was run:
they authenticate as the user, which is past the presence-only scope that was authorised.

ALSO STALE, relevant to any reader of the script: publish-release.sh:5-8 offers "a GRANULAR ACCESS
TOKEN (or classic Automation token)". docs/runbooks/release-publishing.md:557-565 records that npm
permanently revoked every classic token on 9 December 2025, leaving granular tokens as the only type
(90-day cap, 2FA-bound, website-only creation). If the runbook holds, the automation-token option no
longer exists and cannot be chosen.

CHANGE NO CREDENTIAL on this note's account. Credential setup is tier 3 and belongs to the user
directly. Recorded as a fact so attempt four is not spent rediscovering it. Follow-on work: LCLI-489.

AUTH QUESTION SETTLED, 2026-09-14, by the user running the check themselves.

    $ npm whoami
    jeremy-newhouse

That closes the half this record left open. The ~/.npmrc token is VALID, not expired and not
revoked — so the 401-on-expiry theory from the runbook's 2026-08-29 incident does not apply
here. The OTP wall is 2FA-on-write on a token that authenticates fine for reads, which is
exactly what `npm login` produces. The three earlier publish attempts were not fighting a
broken credential; they were fighting the wrong KIND of credential.

Remedy is the user's and is in progress: a granular access token scoped to @opum-ai with
read-and-write, stored in the Keychain under service npm-opum-ai-publish, which is the
first entry in publish-release.sh's load_token() at :104. NOT DONE BY ANY AGENT — credential
setup is tier 3.

STILL UNVERIFIED, and it is the one thing a dry-run cannot test: whether a granular token
bypasses this account's require-2FA-on-write. --dry-run skips both mutating calls, so it
exercises everything EXCEPT the property in question. The real test is the publish. That is
acceptable rather than reckless because the script is fail-closed and ordered: the six
platform packages go first and the root launcher last, so an OTP wall on the first platform
package leaves nothing installable and 0.6.2 stays retryable. Confirmation the token was
picked up at all is the script's own line "auth: using a token (keychain or NPM_TOKEN);
~/.npmrc left untouched" — if it says "falling back to ~/.npmrc" instead, the Keychain entry
is not being found and publishing would hit the same wall again.

Granular tokens are 90-day capped, so this recurs quarterly. The durable fix is OIDC
trusted publishing (LCLI-482).

=== ARTIFACT DIGESTS INDEPENDENTLY VERIFIED FOR THIS RELEASE, not just self-sealed ===

scripts/release-0.6.2/ already holds all 7 tarballs and a SHA256SUMS.txt from the earlier
attempts; `shasum -a 256 -c SHA256SUMS.txt` passes 7/7. On its own that proves only that the
download has not changed since the operator sealed it — the circularity this task and
LCLI-489 both record.

It has now been checked against something CI recorded independently. Each platform's
ladybug-package-qualification-<name>-34801853367-3 artifact carries
package.platformTarballSha256, written by the run itself, and release.yml:492-517 is the job
that asserts it. Recomputed the sha256 of all six platform tarballs on disk and compared:

    darwin-arm64  MATCH        linux-x64     MATCH
    darwin-x64    MATCH        win32-arm64   MATCH
    linux-arm64   MATCH        win32-x64     MATCH

    6/6 match, every report schema lore.ladybug-package-qualification/3, every
    repository.commit = ea3813ae39fd9c9bba1e5e24e32a4c73e1611480 (the v0.6.2 tag).

So the six platform tarballs about to be published are byte-for-byte the artifacts that
passed matching-host qualification on the tagged commit. The ROOT LAUNCHER
(opum-ai-lore-0.6.2.tgz) is NOT covered: it is npm pack'd in that same job and its digest is
recorded nowhere, so for that one the local manifest remains a self-seal. Stated plainly
rather than folded into a "7/7 verified" claim. LCLI-489 carries the fix.

PUBLISH ATTEMPT 4, 2026-09-14 ~06:09Z: FAILED at the first platform package. NOTHING WAS
PUBLISHED and 0.6.2 remains fully retryable -- confirmed by re-querying the registry after
the failure, all seven still ABSENT at 0.6.2 and `latest` still on 0.6.1.

WHAT CHANGED FROM ATTEMPTS 1-3, which is progress rather than a repeat. The granular token
IS being picked up: the run printed "auth: using a token (keychain or NPM_TOKEN); ~/.npmrc
left untouched", so the Keychain path at publish-release.sh:104 now resolves and the
~/.npmrc fallback is out of the picture. All 7 digests verified. Registry reachable.

THE FAILURE IS AUTHORIZATION, NOT 2FA. From the npm debug log:

    http fetch GET 200 https://registry.npmjs.org/@opum-ai%2flore-darwin-arm64
    http fetch PUT 404 https://registry.npmjs.org/@opum-ai%2flore-darwin-arm64

No 401 and no EOTP anywhere in the run. The `otplease` frame in the stack is npm's wrapper,
not an OTP challenge. npm answers 404 rather than 403 on an unauthorized PUT so it does not
disclose package existence -- which is exactly what the script's own banner says a PUT 404
means: the token lacks publish rights on that package.

So the earlier OTP wall and this are DIFFERENT failures. Attempts 1-3 were a web-login token
subject to 2FA-on-write. Attempt 4 is a granular token that authenticates but is not
authorised to write these packages. Do not conflate them in a later summary.

FAIL-CLOSED AND ORDERING BEHAVED EXACTLY AS DESIGNED: the refusal landed on the first
platform package, the root launcher was never attempted, and nothing partial exists to clean
up. This is the second time that design has paid for itself.

MOST LIKELY REMEDY, for the user only -- credential setup is tier 3: on npmjs.com the
granular token's "Packages and scopes" permission must be READ AND WRITE (Read only is the
default and produces precisely this 404), covering the @opum-ai scope or all seven packages
explicitly. Re-add with `security add-generic-password ... -U` and re-run the same command;
the script is resumable and nothing was written.

CORRECTION to the note directly above, same session, 2026-09-14: the Read-only-permission hypothesis is WRONG and was superseded within minutes. A shape check on the stored secret (length and prefix only, no value revealed) returned: length=24, prefix=OTHER, internal_whitespace=no. A granular access token is npm_ + 36 characters = 40. So the Keychain entry under npm-opum-ai-publish does not contain an npm token at all -- something else was stored, or the paste was truncated. That explains the PUT 404 completely without any permissions theory: an unrecognised credential is an unauthenticated write, and npm answers 404. It also explains why the ~/.npmrc fallback disappearing did not help. The remedy is to re-add the correct value (security add-generic-password ... -U, or delete-generic-password first if more than one entry exists) and re-run; the permission settings on npmjs.com may still need checking afterwards, but they are not established as the cause and should not be recorded as one. Recorded because the wrong hypothesis was already written down one note earlier and a reader who stops there would go change token permissions that may be perfectly correct.

PUBLISH ATTEMPT 5, 2026-09-14 ~06:17Z: identical failure, and the shape check explains why. The Keychain secret under npm-opum-ai-publish was re-read immediately after the attempt and is UNCHANGED -- length=24, prefix=OTHER, no whitespace -- so the credential was never replaced between attempts 4 and 5. Exactly one entry exists for that service (acct=jdnewhouse), so this is not the two-entries-and-the-lookup-finds-the-old-one case: `security find-generic-password -s <svc> -w` returns the first match, and here there is only one to return. Nothing published; all seven still ABSENT at 0.6.2, fail-closed held for the third time. Nothing new is wrong -- the token simply has not been swapped yet. When it is, re-run the SAME command; the script is resumable and nothing needs undoing.
finalSummary:
RELEASED 2026-09-14. All seven @opum-ai/lore* packages are live on npm at 0.6.2 with
dist-tags.latest moved on each. Delivered and closed in PR #48; CI run 34814315207 on that
PR's own head. The qualification behind the artifacts is Release run 34801853367 (attempt 3)
on tag v0.6.2 at ea3813ae39fd9c9bba1e5e24e32a4c73e1611480.

EVIDENCE, every line measured against the registry rather than inferred from a publish
command exiting 0:

    npm view @opum-ai/lore dist-tags   ->   { 'release-candidate': '0.3.4', latest: '0.6.2' }
    npx --yes @opum-ai/lore@0.6.2 --version   ->   0.6.2
    all seven packages queried one by one: 0.6.2 present, latest = 0.6.2 on each
    clean-room install (fresh temp dir, nothing from local caches): resolved 0.6.2, the
    launcher's own --version reported 0.6.2, and all six optionalDependencies pinned 0.6.2

HOW IT SHIPPED, and it is not what a reader would assume from 0.6.0: published MANUALLY via
scripts/publish-release.sh 0.6.2 34801853367, against that run's own npm-packages artifact.
The release workflow's OIDC job did not publish it and could not -- LCLI-482 is open and
unresolved. THEREFORE 0.6.2 CARRIES NO PROVENANCE ATTESTATION, and neither did 0.6.1.
Verified directly: `npm view @opum-ai/lore@0.6.2 dist.attestations` returns empty where
0.6.0's returns a SLSA provenance link. A manual publish cannot mint one. This is recorded in
both README.md and docs/reference/lore-cli-release-truth.md so nobody later reads the absence
as tampering.

THE DIGEST CHECK WAS INDEPENDENT FOR SIX OF SEVEN TARBALLS, NOT ALL SEVEN, and this record
says six deliberately. SHA256SUMS.txt is generated by the operator from the same tarballs it
then verifies, which alone proves only that the download has not changed since sealing. The
six PLATFORM tarballs were additionally recomputed and matched against
package.platformTarballSha256 in each ladybug-package-qualification-<name>-34801853367-3
report -- the value release.yml:492-517 asserts -- 6/6, every report carrying
repository.commit = ea3813ae. The ROOT LAUNCHER is npm pack'd in that same job and has no
CI-recorded digest, so its manifest entry remains a local seal. LCLI-489 carries the fix.

WHAT ACTUALLY COST THE TIME, recorded because the tracker's own description was part of it.
Five publish attempts. Attempts 1-3 hit a browser OTP wall; this record claimed auth came
from a granular or automation token in the macOS Keychain, and no such Keychain entry existed
-- the publish was authenticating from ~/.npmrc, the script's last fallback, where a
web-login session is subject to require-2FA-on-write. The description was corrected in place
(PR #44) rather than left to contradict the notes. Attempts 4 and 5 then failed with E404 on
PUT, no OTP and no 401, because the Keychain entry that had since been added held a value
that was not an npm token at all: a length/prefix shape check returned length=24
prefix=OTHER, where a granular token is npm_ + 36 = 40. Fail-closed ordering held all five
times -- every failure landed on the first platform package, the root launcher was never
attempted, and nothing partial ever reached the registry.

The transferable form of all of that is filed on LCLI-489, including the one check that would
have saved two whole attempts: a token shape check costs a second, reveals nothing secret,
and turns a 404 that reads like a permissions problem into an unambiguous "that is not a
token".

DOWNSTREAM NOTIFIED: opum-marketplace (dist-tags.latest has moved so their deliberate hold at
v0.6.1 can lift; skills/ at v0.6.2 is 24277e9a, byte-identical to their existing pin, so the
move needs no re-baseline -- but the NEXT tag resolves to 2998f74d and will), opum-cli-e2e
(re-run the qualification matrix; warned that a provenance assertion will fail for a reason
that is not a release defect, and that the digest scope is six of seven), and quest-cli
(0.6.2 live, plus the shape-check finding and the warning not to adopt npm whoami as a
readiness gate).

GitHub Release v0.6.2 created from CHANGELOG.md's [0.6.2] section: non-draft, non-prerelease,
now marked Latest.
